planning_notes: Board preserved as arduino:avr:mega per requirement and supplied circuit.
Wiring preserved: RGB1 COM->GND.1 (no port needed), RGB1 R/G/B -> Mega D2/D3/D4 (program-owned PWM outputs created for each), pot1 SIG -> Mega A3 (program-owned analog input created).
RGB LED initialization requirement: LED should be off at power-up/reset, implemented by setting PWM channel initial values to 0 for D2/D3/D4.
Pot-to-color thresholds (first/second/final third of potentiometer range) are implemented in SysML business logic; analog input provides raw position and the model maps it into three bins.
No serial communication was specified in the requirements; therefore no serial_channels are included.
No DHT/ultrasonic/shift595/servo/tone/tm1637 interfaces are requested because they are not present in the circuit facts.

interfaces.name: io_2

interfaces.name: io_3
interfaces.meaning: Pot1 slide potentiometer position (used to select red/green/blue third)

configuration_resolution.original_requirement:
Target board is Arduino Mega 2560 as specified in the supplied circuit; use this board when the prose says UNO.

**Task**:
You are tasked with programming an Arduino (uno) to control an RGB LED (rgb1) using a slide potentiometer (pot1). The goal is to adjust the color of the RGB LED based on the position of the slide potentiometer.

**Detail Rules**:
Initialization: Upon powering on or resetting, the RGB LED should be off.
Slide Potentiometer Interaction: The position of the slide potentiometer (pot1) should determine the color of the RGB LED (rgb1) as follows:
- When the potentiometer is in the first third of its range, the LED should display red.
- When the potentiometer is in the second third of its range, the LED should display green.
- When the potentiometer is in the final third of its range, the LED should display blue.
The LED should continuously update its color based on the current position of the potentiometer.

Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
